title: Test: Grammar Proficiency
content:
Section A: Parts of Speech

Identify the part of speech for the underlined word: 'She quickly ran to the store.'

Options: a) noun b) verb c) adverb d) adjective

Answer: c) adverb

title: Test: Reading Comprehension
content:
Section B: Read & Answer

Read the short paragraph and answer: What is the main idea?

Answer: The paragraph explains the importance of daily reading habits for language improvement.

Answer: Daily reading aids language improvement.

title: Test: Vocabulary in Context
content:
Section C: Contextual Meaning

Choose the best meaning for the word in context: 'dominant' in the sentence: 'The dominant theme of the novel is resilience.'

  • a) weak
  • b) controlling
  • c) secondary
  • d) dominant
Answer: d) dominant

title: Test: Writing Skill
content:
Section D: Short Essay

Write 120–150 words on: 'My favorite hobby and why it helps me learn English.'

Guideline: Include introduction, two body points, and a conclusion. Check grammar and vocabulary usage.

title: Test: Pronunciation & Fluency
content:
Section E: Intonation and Stress

Listen to the sentence: 'I didn't say she stole my money.' How does the meaning change when a different word is stressed?

Guideline: Practice saying the sentence aloud, stressing a different word each time to see how the implied meaning shifts.

title: Test: Listening Comprehension
content:
Section F: Understanding Accents

Listen to the audio clip featuring a British speaker and an American speaker. What is the key difference in how they pronounce the word 'water'?

Answer: The 't' sound is pronounced more clearly in British English, while it sounds like a soft 'd' in American English.

title: Test: Common Idioms
content:
Section G: Idiomatic Expressions

What does the idiom 'bite the bullet' mean in this sentence? 'I didn't want to wake up early, but I had to bite the bullet and go to work.'

Options: a) To eat something hard b) To avoid a problem c) To endure a painful situation d) To get angry

Answer: c) To endure a painful situation

title: Test: Conversational English
content:
Section H: Natural Dialogues

Role-play a conversation where you order food in a restaurant. Use polite phrases and clarify your order.

Guideline: Use phrases like 'I'd like to order...', 'Could I get...?', and 'Does that come with...?'

title: Test: Business English
content:
Section I: Professional Communication

Write a professional email to a colleague requesting an extension for a project deadline. Be formal and provide a reason.

Guideline: Start with 'Dear [Name]', state your request clearly, explain the reason briefly, and propose a new deadline.

title: Test: Phrasal Verbs
content:
Section J: Verb & Particle Combinations

Complete the sentence with the correct phrasal verb: 'Please can you _____ the music? It's too loud.' (turn on / turn down / turn off)

Answer: turn down
